answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. This endures because unearned rewards carry forward into the next pool, so even when a farm fails the economy recycles the loss rather than rewarding it. Consider a vault as the anchor of the cost. A sonnet stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a beacon holds the rep...
